messages:
Acme Support: Hi team — after we rolled an egress proxy policy this morning, our services started failing with mTLS handshake errors to the Redwood Private control plane (private.control.redwood.example.com). Errors in our app logs: "tls: handshake failure" and from the client side: "SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL". This started at ~08:15 UTC. Can you help triage? We can share packet captures.

Sam W: Thanks — can you paste a small tcpdump or a hex dump of the ClientHello? Also please try an explicit openssl test from your bastion so we can see the handshake: 
```
openssl s_client -connect private.control.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private.control.redwood.example.com -alpn h2 -tls1_3 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -msg
```

Acme Support: Attaching the minimal tcpdump excerpt (we truncated other traffic). ClientHello shows length 0x?? and then the proxy rewrites something. Snippet: 
```
07:21:03.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.52344 > 52.14.22.99.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 65535, length 511
0000 16 03 01 01 f3 01 00 01 ef 03 03 ... (ClientHello)
...
truncated by upstream: payload length changed -> server never replies with ServerHello
```

Priya N: Can you confirm if your egress proxy/NGFW is doing TLS inspection or any SNI rewriting? Common failure modes are: key_share or extension stripping (TLS1.3), ALPN removal, ClientHello fragmentation (MTU/NAT), or OCSP stapling timeouts. If you can reproduce by bypassing the proxy (egress allowlist) that would be useful. Also please capture the first 512 bytes of the ClientHello hex and paste them.

Acme Support: We verified: when we bypass the proxy by routing the bastion via a different egress path, the openssl s_client command completes successfully and the kube control plane API calls succeed. So this narrows to the inspection path. Here's the first 256 bytes hex of ClientHello from the failing path: 
```
16 03 01 01 f3 01 00 01 ef 03 03 5b 90 ff 1a 2b ... 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
```

Sam W: That pattern (handshake ok when bypassing proxy) strongly indicates the inspection device is modifying the ClientHello. Could you check the proxy TLS-inspection logs for any rule that matches private.control.redwood.example.com and whether it strips unknown extensions? Also confirm your proxy supports TLS1.3 with key_share passthrough — some devices terminate TLS1.3 and re-initiate without exact extension parity which breaks mTLS client cert flows.

Alex R: Two quick repro commands you can run to surface the difference: 
1) failing path (via proxy): 
```
sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/fail.pcap host private.control.redwood.example.com and port 443
openssl s_client -connect private.control.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private.control.redwood.example.com -tls1_3 -msg
```
2) bypass path (works): run same from bastion with direct egress. If the ClientHello on the failing capture is missing key_share or ALPN (h2), the server will either abort or attempt incompatible fallbacks.

Infra Bot: Note: Redwood control plane requires intact ClientHello TLS1.3 extensions for mTLS. Known issues with corporate TLS-inspectors: key_share removal, SNI rewrite/truncation, or re-chunking the TLS record (ClientHello fragmentation). Recommended temporary workaround: add control plane FQDN/IPs to your TLS-inspection bypass/allowlist and allow 443 outbound to the following IP ranges: 52.14.0.0/16, 34.210.0.0/16 (example; contact support for exact ranges). Also ensure ALPN h2 and TLS1.3 are allowed unmodified.

Priya N: If you can share the pcap (redacted) we'll pull the exact ClientHello details. You can also run this quick script to dump extensions: 
```
openssl s_client -connect private.control.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private.control.redwood.example.com -tls1_3 -msg 2>&1 | sed -n '/ClientHello/,/ServerHello/p'
```

Acme Support: Uploaded the pcap to the secure bucket (link sent to support ticket). The capture shows the proxy is collapsing TLS records and removing the key_share extension. Bypassing resolves immediately. We'll add the control plane to our proxy bypass rules as suggested.

Sam W: Great. After you add the bypass, please confirm by rerunning the openssl test and the failing API calls. We'll keep monitoring on our side. We'll also open an internal doc to list the precise control plane IPs and recommend TLS-inspection bypass for mTLS traffic.

Acme Support: Confirmed — after adding allowlist for the control plane IPs and disabling TLS inspection for that destination, the handshake succeeds and service is back to normal. Thanks for the quick help. :tada:

Alex R: Filing a quick follow-up action: update supportKB with a troubleshooting checklist (tcpdump, openssl commands, pcap pointers) and publish recommended allowlist ranges + note about TLS inspection incompatibility with mTLS TLS1.3 key_share behavior. CC @Priya N to draft the KB.

Priya N: Will do, I'll put a short note in docs and link to this thread.

Sam W: Closing loop with customer and marking as resolved in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
